PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Tuple

Tuple has the following attributes:


• The element of the tuple can be of any type.

Source slide page 3 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Tuple

Tuple is a data structure containing zero or more elements.

 Creation of tuple

  •  An empty tuple can be created using a constructor,
        tuplep   ()() or ().()
  •  Tuple with two elements.
         t3 = (1, 2)
  •  Tuple with a single element.
         t3=(1,)

Source slide page 4 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Tuple

• Each element of a tuple can be referred to by a index or a subscript.
• Index is an integer.
Ex:
       >>> t1=(11,22,33,44,55)
       >>> t1[1]
          22
       >>> t1[-1]
           55

Source slide page 5 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Tuple


 • Tuples are immutable. Once created, we cannot change the number of elements
 – no append, no insert, no remove, no delete.



>>> z = (5, 4, 3)
>>> z[2] = 0

Traceback:'tuple' object does not support item

Assignment

Source slide page 6 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Tuple

Benefits of usage of type - Tuple:
• Tuples are faster than lists.
•  If the user wants to protect the data from accidental changes, tuple can be used.
• Tuples can be used as keys in dictionaries, while lists can't.

Source slide page 7 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Tuple


• Elements in the tuple can repeat .

       >>> t1=(11,22,33,44,22,11,55)

• Tuple is a sequence .
• Tuple is also iterable - is eager and not lazy.
         t2=(5,10,15,20)
         for i in t2:
                    print(i, end=' ‘)
• Tuples can be nested. We can have tuple of tuples.
          t=(1,2,3,4,(6,7,8))
         for i in t:
                    print(i)

Source slide page 8 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
 Tuple


• Assignment of one tuple to another causes both to refer to the same tuple.
       >>> t1 = (11, 22, 33, 44, 22, 11, 55)
       >>> t2=t1
       >>> print(id(t1))
              2397027797408
       >>> print(id(t2))
              2397027797408
• tuples can be sliced. This creates a new tuple.
        t1 = (11, 22, 33, 44, 22, 11, 55)
       >>> t1[2:5]
             (33, 44, 22)
       >>> t1[::-1]
             (55, 11, 22, 44, 33, 22, 11)

•  Concatenation:
       Allows us to join two tuples by using operator ‘+’.

Ex:

       >>> tuple1 = (11,33,55,77,99)
      >>> tuple2 = (22,44,66,88,100)
      >>> tuple1 + tuple2
       #concatenates two tuples

Source slide page 14 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
  Tuple

• Repetition:
The repetition operator enables the tuple elements to be repeated multiple
times. The repetition operator requires the first operand to be a tuple and the
second operand to be an integer only.

Ex:

>>> t1=(1,2,3,4)
>>> t1*2
(1, 2, 3, 4, 1, 2, 3, 4)
>>> t1*t1
Traceback (most recent call last):
 File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
TypeError: can't multiply sequence by non-int of type 'tuple

Source slide page 15 (extracted text):
PYTHON FOR COMPUTATIONAL PROBLEM SOLVING
Tuple

Membership Operator:

in and not in

in returns True if a particular item exists in the list. otherwise False
not in operator returns True if the element is not present, otherwise False

Ex:      >>> tup1 = (10,2.2,(22,33,43),(’python’) ) # heterogeneous tuple
         >>> 'python' in tup1
             True
         >>> 'ruby' not in tup1
             True
